alerts.headline: Wind Advisory issued October 26 at 3:36PM HST until October 27 at 6:00AM HST by NWS Honolulu HI
alerts.description:
* WHAT...West winds 30 to 45 mph with gusts up to 60 mph expected.

* WHERE...Big Island Summits.

* WHEN...Until 6 AM HST Tuesday. Summit winds are expected to fall
below advisory level TUesday then increase again Tuesday night and
Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Winds this strong can make driving and walking dangerous.
The winds can forcefully open doors and damage hinges or slam doors
shut, possibly causing injuries.
alerts.instruction:
Use extra caution when driving, especially if operating a high
profile vehicle. Secure outdoor objects.

alerts.headline: Flood Watch issued October 26 at 3:30PM HST until October 29 at 5:00AM HST by NWS Honolulu HI
alerts.description:
A trough moving over the state from the southwest will bring
abundant tropical moisture late Tuesday through at least Wednesday
night. Heavy rain and isolated thunderstorms are expected to produce
flash flooding, and while the greatest flood threat will be focused
over Oahu and Maui County, all islands are at risk.

* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...All main Hawaiian Islands.

* WHEN...From Tuesday morning through late Wednesday night.

* IMPACTS...Significant flooding may occur due to the overflow of
streams and drainages. Roads in several areas may be closed, along
with property damage in urban or low lying spots due to runoff.
Landslides may also occur in areas with steep terrain.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Heavy showers and isolated thunderstorms with intense rain rates
are expected to develop on Tuesday and continue through Wednesday
night as a trough moves over the state. While the greatest flood
threat will be focused over Oahu and Maui County, all islands are
at risk.
alerts.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action
should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.
